title: Driftline Diagnostics — throughput & p95 latency conversation
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
summary: Initial discovery focused on p95 latency goals for streaming clinical summarization, expected concurrency (300–600 active streams), token/sec targets for 2–4k tokens per response, and whether Hosted or Dedicated/Private makes sense given data residency and SOC2 needs.
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark csv + methodology link (hosted vs dedicated) by 2029-01-11
Driftline: provide representative prompt sets and token-length distribution by 2029-01-15
Schedule a 2-hour guided benchmark with Driftline infra (proof-of-concept) week of 2029-01-22
action_items: Maya Chen: email pricing and dedicated capacity commitment tiers + burst options (due 2029-01-11)
Rafael Ortega: prepare streaming p95 test harness and sample k8s load manifest (due 2029-01-18)
Dr. Lila Vance: share 100 anonymized transcripts for eval (due 2029-01-15)
attendees_header: Meeting header: 2029-01-09 / 4pm PT — 52 minutes / Recorded via Fireflies.ai
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um I think we have a hard 50 minutes together so we can cover latency goals and then zoom into concurrency and streaming tests. Can you all quickly introduce?
[00:12] Priya Shah: Sure, Priya Shah CTO at Driftline, we run clinical summarization and a triage assist, we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated for both cost and compliance.
[00:22] Dr. Lila Vance: Lila — head of ML, focusing on model quality, p95 latency matters a lot because clinicians get annoyed with slow responses.
[00:31] Omar Kline: Omar, infra, we care about autoscaling, coldstart and also network egress since PHI is in play.
[00:39] Ben Morales: Ben, SRE, mostly ops questions — how much capacity to reserve and how to failover.
[00:46] Maya Chen: Great — Rafael and Carmen from Redwood will jump into the technicals. Rafael over to you?
[00:51] Rafael Ortega: Thanks. Quick note: I might mis-say product names, sorry in advance — but Redwood has Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. Today let's baseline your p95 target and concurrency profile.
[01:05] Dr. Lila Vance: For our clinical summarizer the desired interactive p95 is 600ms for short notes (~200 tokens) and under 1.2s for full discharge summaries (~2k tokens) — is that realistic on hosted?
[01:20] Rafael Ortega: Okay 600ms p95 for 200 tokens is tight but achievable on optimized small-medium models and with streaming enabled; longer 2k token outputs are dominated by generation time — you'll often be bounded by tokens/sec on the model. For hosted we have latency profiles — do you have a target tokens/sec?
[01:38] Dr. Lila Vance: We'd like 50–100 tokens/sec sustained, bursts up to 400 tokens/sec for some flush jobs.
[01:46] Carmen Li: That's a helpful range. Note that tokens/sec depends on model, quantization, and batch packing. With Dedicated and GPU pools you can tune instance types and get higher tokens/sec, plus predictable p95.
[01:56] Omar Kline: Predictable is key — we don't want noisy neighbors. If we do hosted, will there be performance isolation?
[02:04] Rafael Ortega: Hosted is multi-tenant; we expose performance tiers and concurrency limits. For strict isolation and committed throughput you pick Dedicated where you reserve a GPU pool. Private gives you full network control plus on-prem options.
[02:16] Priya Shah: Data residency — can hosted keep PHI in region and KMS-managed? SOC 2 is required for us.
[02:24] Maya Chen: Yes, hosted supports regional deployments and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; for SOC2-sensitive workflows many customers still choose Dedicated for the additional guarantees and audit logging. We can share SOC2 docs after.
[02:35] Ben Morales: What about token caching — can we cache prefixes? We have a lot of repeat boilerplate.
[02:42] Rafael Ortega: Yes, Redwood supports prefix/KV caching. If your workload repeats common prompts, you can get large token savings and reduced p95. We'll need sample prompt distribution to estimate hit rates.
[02:52] Dr. Lila Vance: We'll provide sample distribution. For concurrency: our peak concurrent active sessions are around 300 now, planning for 600 in 6 months. Each session usually streams while the clinician watches.
[03:04] Carmen Li: Streaming adds complexity — you want to measure p95 end-to-end (first-byte latency) and p95 tail for full response. Which p95 are you tracking?
[03:13] Dr. Lila Vance: First-byte p95 is most critical for perceived latency. Full response p95 can be slower but we'd like it bounded.
[03:20] Rafael Ortega: Good. For streaming first-byte p95 600ms is in range with dedicated tuned models and caching. For hosted we can probably hit it under typical loads but you'd see variance under burst.
[03:30] Priya Shah: Can you run an audit test: 300 concurrent streams with 200-token median length, 10% 2k tokens, measure first-byte and 95th tail?
[03:40] Rafael Ortega: Absolutely — we can run a guided benchmark. Couple of clarifying q's: what model family do you expect to use — open Llama variants, or a smaller supervised model?
[03:50] Dr. Lila Vance: We're evaluating a v1.2 of a fine-tuned 13B open model, quantized to 4-bit for latency.
[03:58] Omar Kline: We're also interested in mixed workloads: embeddings for search and generation together on the same route. How does Redwood route that?
[04:06] Carmen Li: We recommend separate routes for embeddings and generation but you can colocate on Dedicated if you want lower egress. Our routing can prioritize latency SLOs and fallback to smaller quantized variants when overloaded.
[04:17] Ben Morales: About fallbacks — if the primary model misses p95 during a surge, what's the automatic flow?
[04:23] Rafael Ortega: Policy-based routing: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a lower-cost/low-latency variant. We can set thresholds (like 95th > 1.5x SLO) to trigger fallback.
[04:33] Dr. Lila Vance: For clinical accuracy though, fallback models must not change outputs dramatically. We need to evaluate hallucination risk.
[04:40] Rafael Ortega: Agreed — we do quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evaluation prompts. For critical paths you can pin a model version and schedule gradual rollouts.
[04:50] Priya Shah: Can you talk about autoscaling — cold starts are a big worry for us.
[04:55] Rafael Ortega: Dedicated supports warm pools and pre-warmed workers. Autoscaling is configurable with cooldowns; Private gives you total control — but you pay for reserved nodes. Hosted has faster vertical scaling but some coldstart variance during large regional surges.
[05:09] Omar Kline: How do we benchmark coldstart impact on p95 for streaming?
[05:14] Rafael Ortega: Typical technique: measure rolling p95 with synthetic ramp that introduces new sessions periodically, and track p95 delta when new workers are provisioned. We'll produce a script and k8s manifest to reproduce.
[05:24] Dr. Lila Vance: About quantization: we plan to run 4-bit. Do you have experience trade offs: throughput vs accuracy?
[05:31] Carmen Li: Yes, 4-bit quantization usually increases tokens/sec significantly but may slightly affect logits — your fine-tune can be robust, but we'll run A/B comparison on held-out prompts. Sometimes dynamic mixed-precision helps.
[05:42] Ben Morales: Any guidance on GPU types for 13B quantized?
[05:45] Rafael Ortega: For 13B 4-bit you can get good throughput on A100-40 or equivalent; for cost optimization cheap cards are possible but less throughput. Dedicated pools let you choose hardware or Redwood can recommend profiles for your token/sec target.
[05:58] Priya Shah: For regulatory reasons we might consider Private in a VPC — how different is the operational model?
[06:05] Maya Chen: Private deployment provides a customer-managed control plane with audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, KMS support, and optional on-prem package. It adds operational overhead but gives you full network isolation and residency.
[06:17] Omar Kline: How about backup routing — multi-region failover?
[06:21] Rafael Ortega: We support multi-region pinning and cross-region failover, with automatic fallback to compatible variants in another region if capacity or region fails. That is part of Dedicated and Hosted multi-region offerings.
[06:33] Priya Shah: Could you run a cost exemplar: hitting 300 concurrent streams at 50 tokens/sec for 10 minutes average, compare hosted vs dedicated?
[06:44] Maya Chen: We'll provide a model and cost spreadsheet, but quick estimate: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, which can be higher per-token at scale. Dedicated gives lower unit cost for sustained throughput but requires commitment. We'll send concrete numbers.
[06:58] Dr. Lila Vance: For the benchmark, please include wall-clock p95 for first-byte and full response, tokens/sec median and 95th, and GPU util numbers.
[07:07] Rafael Ortega: Yep — we'll instrument token throughput, latency percentiles, and per-route CPU/GPU utilization. We'll also dump KV cache hit rates if you opt-in.
[07:15] Ben Morales: Security: SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit trails — what's available?
[07:20] Maya Chen: SSO with SAML/OIDC, RBAC for team roles, audit logs for every request (can be forwarded), and enterprise keys via KMS/HSM on Private. We'll share our security pack link.
[07:32] Priya Shah: Ok great. Can you call out risks we should be aware of?
[07:36] Rafael Ortega: Main risks: model regression on quantization; burst-induced latency spikes on hosted; network egress for PHI; and fallback model quality drift. We'll mitigate with staged benching, regressions, and pinned versions.
[07:48] Dr. Lila Vance: For our internal success criteria: 600ms first-byte p95 for 200-token responses under 300 concurrent streams, and full response within 1.2s for 2k tokens at 95th. If you can consistently hit that we'll pilot.
[08:03] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll target that benchmark. Rafael, Carmen, align on test plan?
[08:09] Rafael Ortega: I'll outline test parameters: model variant, quantization level, traffic shape, warm-start percentage, and metrics to collect.
[08:16] Carmen Li: We'll include a step to validate semantic parity between fallback and primary with a small eval set.
[08:21] Omar Kline: How long does a guided benchmark take to schedule and run?
[08:25] Rafael Ortega: Setup usually 2–3 working days to provision and 1–2 days to run tests, then 1 day to analyze. So a week end-to-end typically.
[08:36] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Any legal/procurement blockers? We will need contract language for Dedicated commitments.
[08:42] Maya Chen: We'll loop in sales ops after this call — pricing and term options will be follow-up.
[08:47] Ben Morales: One more operational: observability. We need per-token cost breakdowns and per-route p95 dashboards.
[08:55] Carmen Li: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We can demo console in the next call.
[09:04] Dr. Lila Vance: Can you also provide a checklist for Private? We want to evaluate that path in parallel.
[09:10] Rafael Ortega: Sure — we'll provide a Private evaluation checklist (network, KMS, audit, on-prem footprint).
[09:16] Priya Shah: Ok let's move to quick Q/A from the team.
[09:20] Omar Kline: Do you support custom kernel optimizations for quantized models?
[09:24] Rafael Ortega: Yes, the runtime picks optimized kernels and we can surface kernel-level differences in the benchmark artifacts.
[09:29] Ben Morales: How do you handle tokenization differences between model forks?
[09:33] Carmen Li: We harmonize tokenizers in the pipeline and include tokenization pre-processing in the harness so the benchmarks reflect production behavior.
[09:41] Dr. Lila Vance: Any surprising caveats others have seen in streaming-heavy clinical apps?
[09:46] Rafael Ortega: Two: long-tail requests that generate >4k tokens can starve throughput unless you isolate those routes; and embedding + generation colocated may cause interference unless you partition resources.
[09:58] Maya Chen: Good note. We'll recommend separate routes for heavy open-ended generation.
[10:03] Priya Shah: Ok that covers most. Let's recap and deadlines.
[10:08] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send benchmark methodology and hosted vs dedicated cost spreadsheet by Jan 11; Driftline to provide sample prompt set and token dist by Jan 15; we schedule a 2-hr guided benchmark week of Jan 22.
[10:21] Dr. Lila Vance: Correct. Also please include SOC2 doc link and the Private checklist.
[10:28] Maya Chen: Will do. Anything else?
[10:31] Ben Morales: No, thanks — appreciate the detail.
[10:35] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone.
[10:38] Rafael Ortega: Thanks team — we will follow up with concrete artifacts.
[10:42] Maya Chen: End meeting.

Notes: transcript includes some transcription artifacts; product names occasionally simplified (Dedicated -> Dedicate in quick speech). References shared: benchmark csv (link will be emailed), security pack (link to SSO/KMS docs), guided benchmark manifest (to be shared).
